The 1.8.24 service had been drained; VS Code (with the 1.8.29 extension's `airkctl session`, PID 19248) was still open. A temporary live probe (not committed) a minute later found a complete scan (414 processes, 0 unobserved), so the miss was transient during the drain. **Root cause:** `legacy_processes` (Windows) counted a failed `QueryFullProcessImageNameW` or a failed owner lookup on an opened process as a miss even when that process had exited mid-scan (the 1.8.26 fix excused only exits before `OpenProcess`), and `setup_role::effects::await_sessions` refused on the first incomplete scan instead of observing again inside its 15 s window, during exactly the period when drained processes exit. **Fix:** after such a failure the open handle's `GetExitCodeProcess` decides; only an observed exit code other than `STILL_ACTIVE` excuses it (pure `still_running`), and the open handle keeps the PID from reuse for the owner lookup; `await_sessions` uses pure `session_wait` (done only on a complete scan with no running image; otherwise observe again until the unchanged deadline; at the deadline a running image is reported first as `installation_files_in_use`, else `process_observation_incomplete`). No deadline or budget widened. **Evidence:** Clippy `-p airk-cli` (83 s, pass); T0 `scan-race-t0` 69/69 (`legacy_processes::`, `setup_role::`, `runtime_install::replacement::`) including `a_failed_query_is_excused_only_by_an_observed_exit` and `an_incomplete_scan_is_observed_again_until_the_deadline`; the probe's audit through the new code: complete, 409 scanned. **Not reproduced:** the exact exiting process was not captured (the scan does not record which PID missed); the fix covers every exit-race path in the loop. **Advice to the user for 1.8.29:** close every VS Code window and rerun the installer; retirement is done and nothing is draining now. |
| Upgrade with VS Code open: I4 replacement notice; download links (user request, 12 Nov) | source done; installer 1.8.30 | **Question (user):** why must every VS Code window close, and will new installs require it? **Answer recorded:** only an upgrade/repair/uninstall of an installed service required it: each window's `airkctl session` runs the installed `airkctl.exe`, Windows cannot overwrite a running image, setup may not terminate it (Â§9.6.2) and the session survives a service stop to reconnect. A fresh install has no installed image and never waited. **Request (user):** fix it all, robustly, as 1.8.30; point the VSIX description and Explorer at the downloads page. **Design (primary, under the standing authorization):** the Â§9.6 phase-3 "drain affected CLI sessions" is implemented with an I4 file, not an I1/I2 wire change: contract step `ReplacementNotice` (`airk-install-replacing/1`, `replacing.json` beside the pointer, canonical, 4 KiB, lifetime â‰¤ 10 min, decoded against the caller's clock; new refusals `replacement_notice_expired`, `replacement_notice_lifetime_too_long`; fixture section `replacement_notices`, 11 reviewed cases in `i4_cases.py`). Setup writes it in `drain` before `Shutdown` when installed images exist and the step places or removes files, keeps it through placement and removes it when the receipt closes (complete or failed); expiry covers a killed installer. ## Split completion (12 November 2026)

**Report (user, 1.8.30 manual install):** no way to create an index from the
Explorer; Indexing shows `catalog_control_connection_unavailable`. The user
asked for the split plan to be finished properly and a 1.8.31 installer and
VSIX built. Plan approved with U97 (read-only Explorer Indexing plus Open AIRK
Admin, in VS Code or the browser), U98 (typed destructive confirmation) and U99
(selection Q2â€“Q5; 1.8.31 Windows-only).

**Why it fails (source review, no runs):** `AirkctlExplorerHost`
(`packages/vscode/src/airkctl/features/explorerHost.ts`) supplies a read-only
`ControlSource` with no catalog methods and none of the window-context, scope,
prefill, usage or handoff host members, so `ExplorerControl.catalog` is
undefined and every Indexing action throws at `indexingCatalogController.ts`
`run`. Index setup moved to the admin pages (U6), but `packages/admin` has no
Index library or Usage page; the admin plane fills only top-level request keys
(`admin_plane/mutations.rs` `KEYED`), so nested catalog keys
(`IndexSetupSelection.key`, `CatalogRequest.caller/key`) cannot be produced;
destructive rows are refused for want of a confirmation form; storage and
login rows are deferred; admin search and window reads wait for selection
authority. `airkctl` has no catalog/index/set/grant/plan/storage/login
commands, against the P0 decision; `service rpc` was the only route.

**Gap map:** admin pages (missing Index library and index sets, Usage; Storage,
Recovery execute, login startup, resources, Overview version/leftovers, plans,
events stream, search and evidence under the admin grant, `packages/ui`);
admin rows (nested keys, U98, source/grant/split-recover/setup-resume/usage
rows, rate limits, semaphore, coverage test); selection authority Step C, S1
(W4), S2 (A2); `airkctl` management commands and `admin open|url --page`;
extension host wiring (window context, W4 scope, prefill, Workbench toggle,
Assistance subscription, handoffs), webview (read-only Indexing, admin
opener, removal of `manage`/`usage`/`runtimeUpgrade`/split UI), Workbench
scope picker, deletion of modules that leave the extension, parity through
the real session transport; known failing tests (`publishing.test`,
`a_missing_installation_or_service_exits_three`) and harness scripts still on
the old `airk` CLI; no scripted T2 installed-product run.

## Workers patch review (10 November 2026, read-only)

**Confirmed from source:**

1. A query past its 125 s deadline calls `process::exit(75)`, which now ends the whole service.
2. Drain only works inside `service_execution::run`. A slow startup or activation, or a blocking read, leads to exit 76, and recovery replays the work, so every project goes into a crash loop.
3. On early `?` returns, the cleanup owner exits without joining its job.
4. The stall watchdog restarts the whole service.
5. PDF slot outcomes are misclassified: busy is treated as a fatal job failure, and an interruption marks the document as disappeared.
6. Usage spans see whole-service counters.
7. A poisoned shared cache affects every project, and cache notification handles outlive their owner.
8. `ChildWorker::drop` can block the supervisor.
9. On Unix, the PDF child can be orphaned after a service crash.
10. `scripts/check-self-spawn.py` has false negatives.

**Plausible risks:**

- the watcher memory check is gone;
- exit 76 during stop/upgrade;
- callers that turn a checkpoint into a bool can continue past a drain;
- the production in-process start path is not covered by native tests.

- workers agent: items 1â€“4, 8, 10, 11 and 13;
- PDF agent: items 5 and 9;
- caches and usage agent: items 6 and 7.

**Item 12, `scripts/check-self-spawn.py`: implemented, Python T0 passed.**

- A `;` inside a signature (`[u8; 4]`) ended the function early.
- `br"â€¦"` raw strings were not recognized.
- A role literal in a const was skipped.

Correction:

**Items 6 and 7 (caches and usage agent): implemented, not compiled.**

- **Usage spans.** The epoch advances on every start and end. Disabled-usage requests are counted as unmeasured work. A new `airk_kernel::OwnerActivity` guard covers owner work, and a poisoned tracker lock is recovered and reported as overlapped. Reporting goes through the existing `ResourceMeasurement.overlapped` / `ResourceSummary.overlapped_intervals` fields; there is no wire change.
- **Caches.** Poison recovery and per-collection release for `verified_cache`, `lexical/cache` (change-notification handles) and kernel `source_policy` `RUNTIMES`, the latter for expired bindings only.
- **New public items:** `airk_kernel::{OwnerActivity, release_collection_caches}` and `airk_store::current::release_collection_caches`.
- **Integrator wiring is pending** until the workers agent finishes: `OwnerActivity` in `service_execution::run` and in the source watcher, and release at project/cleanup owner exit.
- **Recorded risk:** more spans report as overlapped and carry no counters.

**Items 5 and 9 (PDF agent): implemented, not compiled; the Unix code is uncompiled.**

- A busy slot defers the document: its previous artifact stands in under an unchanged binding, it gets one retry at the next drain, and is then recorded with the `extraction_deferred` skip code.
- An interrupted wait stops the scan with the typed `PdfSlotInterrupted`, settling nothing.
- Unix parent death: Linux `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` plus a `getppid` re-check; macOS kqueue `NOTE_EXIT`. The decision rule is a pure `parent_watch`.
- Bounds: 60 s slot wait per attempt, at most two waits per document per scan, a 15 s / 10 s CPU / 512 MiB parse.

Integrator follow-ups:

**Items 1â€“4, 8, 10, 11 and 13 (workers agent): implemented.**

- `StopStep::Quarantine` replaces `ExitService`; `exit_service_for_stuck_owner` is removed.
- Stopping owners are polled from a thread-local `STOPPING` list on the actor's turn. `ChildWorker::drop` never waits for an in-process owner.
- The query deadline and the stall watchdog quarantine the owner's own scope. Only a child-process fixture still exits 75/76.
- The lease is held in `WorkerScope` until the owner thread returns.

**Integrator integration (primary), source-reviewed:**

- **`catalog.rs` `DrainWorker`.** It relied on the old blocking `Drop`. It now returns a typed `WorkerDrainPending` while the owner is in `STOPPING`, and `CatalogControlHandle::drain_worker` asks again for up to 35 s (stop grace + drain + 5 s). After that it fails as quarantined.
- **`service_execution::run`.** It holds `OwnerActivity`, and maps `PdfSlotInterrupted` to the owner's `Draining`/`Canceled`/`WorkStalled`; if no flag is set, the original error is kept.
- **Cache release.** `worker_scope::CollectionCaches`, a drop guard calling `airk_kernel::release_collection_caches`, is placed right after the registration in `project_worker::serve` and `derived_worker::serve`, so it drops after the kernels and the job.
- **Decision: the source watcher is not registered as `OwnerActivity`.** Marking its 250 ms pulses would make nearly every span overlapped. Residual: the watcher's own CPU can still land in a concurrent span.
- **Shutdown with a quarantined owner was checked.** `ChildWorker::drop` returns without joining, and the actor loop ends once every remaining owner is quarantined.
- **Docs filled in.** `process-model.md`, `release-1.8.21.md` and `service-progress.md:22` now have the real field names, codes and bounds. The drafted "typed stuck-owner status observation" was corrected: status uses the existing `automatic_start_blocked` and cannot tell a quarantine apart from an exhausted circuit; the reason is in the service log. A distinct status field would be a D8 contract change, left to the user.

Lock correction (`runtime_install.rs`):

- `existing_install_lock` stays exclusive, because `inspect-legacy-caches` can settle an interrupted withdrawal. It now waits for a held lock up to `EXISTING_INSTALL_LOCK_WAIT` (15 s) before refusing, through `existing_install_lock_within(root, budget, pause)` with an injected pause.

**The `native_owner_recovery` Ã—3 failures are a fixture ACL problem, not a code defect.** They come from the partial `integ-tests-r1.log` (`native Windows boundary policy unavailable`).

- Cause: the runner's `native-fixtures/` directory inherits the repository ACL, which includes Authenticated Users with Modify rights. The native private-boundary check rightly refuses that.
- The documented precondition (release-readiness.md, "native-fixtures") is a directory with FullControl for only the creator, SYSTEM and Administrators. `readiness-1820/native-fixtures` has the same broad ACL.
- Correction: a new directory, `artifacts/one-process/native-fixtures-private/`, has its inheritance removed and those three grants. No existing ACL was changed.
- `integ-tests-r2` passes `--fixture-base artifacts/one-process/native-fixtures-private`.

Open for the user: the Explorer Assistance start (`explorer_assistance::command`) runs VS Code's Node runtime for an external agent. It is not an `airk.exe` process, but it is a per-agent process.

**Integrator design decision:** quarantine replaces the service exit. A stuck owner keeps its lease, its project's circuit opens and its status reports the problem; other projects keep running, and an explicit restart is the recovery. The full correction batch was returned to the workers owner, who now works in the main checkout.

### Advanced split P7/P8 original-operation wrapper recovery

Standalone Linux/macOS wrappers now accept `--resume <absolute original operation-request.json>` without option or location overrides. Inno placing recovery uses `/AIRKOPERATION`; native-success finalization recovery skips native replay but still completes PATH and EXE/DAT sealing. Inno removal also accepts its verified retained image and resumes outer tracked-file/registry cleanup even after native removal completed and the placed service image disappeared. Native-owned scalar projection (`--recovery-field`) is coordinated with the setup owner; shells/Pascal do not decode or rewrite I4. The native projection/admission/reconciliation tests remain the native owner's responsibility; wrapper fixture passes do not qualify actual installed journeys. Portable instructions now document the existing portable-only public CLI `service setup --resume ... --portable`.
